text.p: Here are highlights of stories in Romania's press on Friday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy:
Business:
ADEVARUL
- Reform Minister Ulm Spineanu is determined to go ahead with plans to close down loss-making companies.
- Prime Minister Victor Ciorbea is quoted as saying that wage indexation will start in August.
- Floods in recent days caused losses worth 200 billion lei, the paper says.
- Managers of several loss-making companies protest aginst government plans to close down inefficient firms.
- The visiting IMF experts in Bucharest do not endorse Romania's plans to build 96 Cobra attack helicopter worth some two billion dollars, the paper says.
- The troubled private Dacia Felix bank needs around 200 billion lei to recover, the paper says.
ROMANIA LIBERA
- Romania's big trade unions walked out of talks with the government on pay issues.

- The World Bank opposes plans by the government to create a new national oil company grouping three refineries. The World Bank suggested the new firm should operate only one refinery, the paper says.
- The government decided to give farmers a bonus worth 150,000 lei per tonne of wheat in a bid to encourage exports.
- The state-run Tarom airline appointed a new management.
- The Banca Agricola commercial bank will be restructured ahead of its privatisation, bank president Liviu Marica is quoted as saying.
CURIERUL NATIONAL
- Harvesting of Romania's 1997 wheat crop is affected by lack of equipment and funds, the paper quotes Trita Fanita, head of the Senate's committee for agriculture, food and forestry, as saying.
General:
CURIERUL NATIONAL
- Romania's population will fall until the year 2025 and the average age of the population will rise, the newspaper said quoting officials of the National Center of Demographic Research.
ROMANIA LIBERA

- The war of flags in Transylvanyan city of Cluj continues, the paper said. It presents various reactions after the mayor's failure to remove the Hungarian flag at the Hungarian consulate opened in Cluj last week.
ADEVARUL
The newspaper presents a full-page report on the miners' strike 20 years ago in the Jiu Valley under the communist regime.
-- Bucharest newsroom 40-1 3120264
